title_en: Mao Dexian, Chengxian Ciba Xumishan Industrial Co., Ltd., No. 106 Team of Gansu Nonferrous Metal Geological Exploration Bureau, and Chengxian Hengxing Mining Co., Ltd. v. Baiyin Nonferrous Metals Company — dispute over mining rights
ruling_gist_en: 1. Pursuant to Article 7 of the Administrative Penalty Law of the PRC, if a citizen, legal person, or other organization has been subjected to an administrative penalty for an illegal act, and such illegal act causes damage to others, they shall bear civil liability in accordance with the law. full_text_en:
Mao Dexian, Chengxian Ciba Xumishan Industrial Co., Ltd., 
No.106 Team of Gansu Nonferrous Metals Geological Exploration Bureau, 
Chengxian Hengxing Mining Co., Ltd. 
v. 
Baiyin Nonferrous Metals Company 
— Dispute over mining rights

【Ruling Summary】

1. Pursuant to Article 7 of the Administrative Penalty Law of the People's Republic of China, where a citizen, legal person, or other organization is subject to an administrative penalty for illegal acts that cause damage to others, it shall bear civil liability in accordance with the law. Where a person, through fault, infringes upon the civil rights and interests of another, he shall bear corresponding tort liability. The fact that the person has already been subjected to an administrative penalty for the same act does not affect his assumption of civil liability.

2. Pursuant to Article 2 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Proceedings, a party shall bear the responsibility to provide evidence to prove the facts on which its claims are based or to rebut the facts on which the opposing party's claims are based. Where there is no evidence or the evidence is insufficient to prove the factual allegations of the party, the party bearing the burden of proof shall bear the adverse consequences. Where a party maliciously obstructs investigation and evidence collection during the case investigation and handling process, causing the investigating authority to be unable to obtain relevant evidence, that party shall bear the legal consequences of failure to adduce evidence.

3. Where a person infringes upon the property of another and causes losses, he shall bear liability for damages. In particular, the costs incurred in an act of maliciously infringing upon state-owned assets are different from the costs in general civil transactions, and such costs shall not be deducted when calculating the amount of infringement losses.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court of the People's Republic of China
(2011) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 22

The appellants Mao Dexian, Chengxian Ciba Xumishan Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xumishan Company), No.106 Team of Gansu Nonferrous Metals Geological Exploration Bureau (hereinafter referred to as No.106 Team), and Chengxian Hengxing Mining Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hengxing Company), in the case of dispute over mining rights against the respondent Baiyin Nonferrous Metals Company (hereinafter referred to as Baiyin Company), dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2008) Gan Min Er Chu Zi No. 15 rendered by the Gansu High People's Court, appealed to this Court. This Court, by civil ruling (2009) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 144 dated March 24, 2010, remanded the case to the Gansu High People's Court for retrial. After retrial, the Gansu High People's Court rendered civil judgment (2010) Gan Min Er Chu Zi No. 15 on September 8, 2010. Mao Dexian, Xumishan Company, No.106 Team, and Hengxing Company, all dissatisfied, appealed to this Court. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel composed of Presiding Judge Wang Chuang, Judge Li Jingping, and Acting Judge Wang Fubo to hear the case. Court Clerk Shang Min served as recorder. The case is now concluded.

The original trial court found through trial that:

No.106 Team, as a specialized institution under the Gansu Provincial Geological Exploration Bureau responsible for the geological exploration of the Lijiagou lead-zinc mine, submitted the "Geological Exploration Report on the Lijiagou Lead-Zinc Deposit in Chengxian County, Gansu Province" to the National Mineral Reserves Committee in March 1986. On January 5, 1988, the National Mineral Reserves Committee formally approved the "Geological Exploration Report on the Lijiagou Lead-Zinc Deposit in Chengxian County, Gansu Province" submitted by No.106 Team of Gansu Nonferrous Metals Geological Exploration Company. The ore grade, specific gravity calculation methods, and orebody occurrences of the three illegal stopes involved in this case, namely Orebody I, Orebody III2 at Line 105, and Orebody III2 at Line 109, are specifically recorded and described in this report.

On September 2, 1998, Baiyin Company obtained the Mining License with certificate number 1000009820009 issued by the Ministry of Land and Resources. The license states: the mining license is valid from September 1998 to September 2013, with a production scale of 660,000 tons per year, a mining area of 1.44 square kilometers, and a mining depth elevation of 1375-700 meters. The coordinates of the boundary points are: 1. 3756848 (X), 35563555 (Y); 2. 3756500 (X), 35563810 (Y); 3. 3757000 (X), 35565410 (Y); 4. 3757335 (X), 35565500 (Y); 5. 3757765 (X), 35564810 (Y); 6. 3758065 (X), 35564885 (Y); 7. 3758175 (X), 35564590 (Y); 8. 3757300 (X), 35564130 (Y); 9. 3757000 (X), 35563855 (Y). Upon comparison, it is determined that the three stopes involved, namely Orebody I, Orebody III2 at Line 105, and Orebody III2 at Line 109, fall within the area delineated by the above nine boundary points; the mining area delineated by the above nine boundary points neither intersects nor overlaps with the area delineated by the 15 boundary points stated in the mining license held by Xumishan Company.

On October 22, 2006, while conducting inspection and monitoring of a civilian mining adit at Wangjiagou within its jurisdiction area, Baiyin Company discovered newly welded and sealed steel gratings near the geological exploration line 102 of Orebody III2. The next day, after removing the gratings, Baiyin Company found a large-scale cross-border mining area. Over thirty workers of the defendants were engaged in large-scale illegal mining activities in the area of Orebody I belonging to Baiyin Company. Three workers from Huangzhu Beneficiation Plant, namely Lai Dingyi, Lai Dingcheng, and Su Shiyun, who were carrying out the illegal mining, were caught on site. Under the guidance of these three workers, the illegal mining site was inspected on site, and video was recorded simultaneously. On the same day, Baiyin Company reported the matter to the relevant administrative authorities. On October 28, 2006, the Longnan Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources and the Chengxian County Bureau of Land and Resources formed a joint investigation team of the city and county and rushed to the illegal mining area for on-site field investigation. On November 24, 2006, led by the Gansu Provincial Department of Land and Resources, a joint investigation team composed of provincial, municipal, and county governments and various functional departments was again formed to investigate the illegal mining by the defendants.

During the investigation, the investigation team commissioned surveyors from Baiyin Company to conduct actual measurements of the three illegal stopes discovered on the 23rd: 1. In the Orebody I area, a stope approximately 80.6 meters long had been formed, using shallow hole ore extraction; there were 9 short crosscuts for ore removal, ore extraction height reached 10 meters, average mining width 7 meters, and mining had progressed to near geological exploration line 97. 2. Near Line 105 of Orebody III2, an inclined upward raise, downward inclined shaft, large car yard, tunnels, a large number of 0.75 cubic meter mine cars, and relatively complete and standardized ventilation, air supply, power supply, water supply, communication, and transportation systems were discovered, forming a stope with a height of 6 meters, mining width of 3 meters, and stope length of 50 meters. 3. In the cross-border mining area at elevation 1190m of Orebody III2, there was a stope with a length of 30m, width of 6-8m, height of 16m, with 5 ore outlets, ore grade above 10%, and the blasted ore had been basically removed. The investigation team took on-site photos of the illegal mining situation. On November 23, 2006, based on the investigation team's instructions and actual measurement results, Baiyin Company prepared an actual measurement data report and horizontal plan maps of the three illegal stopes. According to these measurement results, the illegally mined ore volume for Orebody I (Line 97 stope) was 14,508 tons; for Orebody III2 (Line 105 stope) was 2,700 tons; for Orebody III2 (Line 109 stope) was 10,080 tons. The total ore loss from the three stopes was 27,288 tons.

In October 2006, five special VAT invoices from transactions between Baiyin Company and third parties showed the zinc concentrate transaction prices for that period as RMB 21,954/ton, RMB 21,971/ton, RMB 22,831/ton, RMB 21,971/ton, and RMB 21,992/ton, with an average price of RMB 22,143.8/ton. Two special VAT invoices from transactions between Baiyin Company and third parties in October 2006 showed the lead concentrate transaction prices for that period as RMB 11,380/ton, RMB 11,440/ton, RMB 11,380/ton, and RMB 11,340/ton, with an average price of RMB 11,385/ton.

Between November 23 and November 30, 2006, the investigation team verified that the entity responsible for the cross-border mining was the Xumingshan Lead-Zinc Mine of Xumishan Company. The cross-border mining area was from Line 102 to Line 109 of Orebody III2 (including two locations: Orebody III2 at Line 105 and Orebody III2 at Line 109) and the area around Line 97 of Orebody I.

On November 7, 2006, the Chengxian County Bureau of Land and Resources of Gansu Province issued Document Chengguozi [2006] No. 153, "Notice on Again Ordering the Clearance and Dredging of the Mining Adit at Qijiagou Estuary," requiring Xumishan Company to completely dredge its mining adit by November 11. On November 20, 2006, the Bureau again issued Document Chengguozi [2006] No. 160, "Notice on Accelerating the Clearance and Dredging of the Mining Adit at Qijiagou Estuary," stating: "Our Bureau has twice notified your mine on October 31 and November 7, 2006, to clear and dredge all collapsed and blocked sections within the mining adit and submit a written report on the clearance situation, but your mine has not yet reported on the clearance. We again notify your mine to dredge the adit within three days of receiving this notice."

On November 25, 2006, the First Institute of Geology and Mineral Resources Exploration of Gansu Provincial Bureau of Geology and Mineral Resources Exploration and Development (hereinafter referred to as the First Institute) conducted an estimation of resource volume in the mined-out areas involved and issued the "Report on Estimation of Resource Volume in the Mined-Out Areas of Changba Lead-Zinc Mine at Line 97 and Line 105 (Elevation 1190m)" (hereinafter referred to as the "Estimation Report"). The report estimated two parts: "I. Stope at Line 105 (Elevation 1190), II. Stope at Line 97." By comparison with the three illegal mining locations claimed by Baiyin Company: 1. The "I. Stope at Line 105 (Elevation 1190)" part of the report actually corresponds to the Orebody III2 at Line 109 claimed by Baiyin Company. 2. The "II. Stope at Line 97" part of the report actually corresponds to the Orebody I claimed by Baiyin Company. The report stated that "the Line 97 stope could not be inspected on site due to blockage." 3. The Orebody III2 at Line 105 claimed by Baiyin Company was not mentioned in the report.

On November 28, 2006, Mao Dexian signed and confirmed the "Cross-Border Mining Investigation Plan Map," which was also stamped with the official seal of Huangzhu Beneficiation Plant for confirmation.

On September 13, 2007, the Longnan Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources issued Document Longguozifa [2007] No. 2, "Administrative Penalty Decision on Mineral Resources," imposing an administrative penalty on Xumishan Company for having, since 2006, exceeded the approved mining area and entered the Lijiagou mining area in violation of relevant regulations: "1. Confiscate the illegally mined ore volume of 4,907 tons, equivalent to RMB 1,048,135; 2. Impose a fine of 5% of the illegal income, amounting to RMB 52,407." From Evidence Seven submitted by Hengxing Company, it appears that the administrative penalty determined the illegally mined ore volume of 4,907 tons consisted of two parts: first, the ore volume of 2,005.36 tons from Orebody III2 at Line 109 as found in the Estimation Report; second, 2,901.6 tons, which is 20% of the 14,508 tons from Orebody I at Line 97 claimed by Baiyin Company.

On October 27, 2008, Baiyin Company filed a lawsuit with the original trial court claiming that its owned Lijiagou Lead-Zinc Mine, located in Huangzhu Town, Chengxian County, Gansu Province, was issued Mining License No. 1000009820009 by the Ministry of Land and Resources on September 2, 1998, valid from September 1998 to September 2013. On October 22, 2006, while monitoring a civilian mining adit at Wangjiagou within its jurisdiction area, Baiyin Company discovered cross-border mining activities in the area near geological exploration lines 102 and 105 of Orebody III2 and near line 97 of Orebody I, and immediately reported to government departments at all levels, requesting an investigation. From November 23 to November 30 of the same year, the Gansu Provincial Department of Land and Resources, together with the Gansu Provincial Administration of Work Safety, Longnan Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources, Longnan Municipal Administration of Work Safety, Chengxian County People's Government, Chengxian County Bureau of Land and Resources, and other relevant units, formed a joint investigation team to conduct an on-site investigation of the cross-border mining situation. The investigation determined that the entity responsible for the cross-border mining was the Xumingshan Lead-Zinc Mine of Xumishan Company, and the cross-border mining area was from Line 102 to Line 109 of Orebody III2 and the area around Line 97 of Orebody I. According to calculations, the mined ore volume was 27,288 tons. The Xumingshan Lead-Zinc Mine of Xumishan Company was jointly owned by three defendants. On November 24, 2003, Huangzhu Beneficiation Plant, Xumishan Company, and No.106 Team signed the "Joint Exploration Agreement," incorporating the "Gansu Chengxian Ciba Xumishan Lead-Zinc Mine Survey" project, with the three parties holding exploration proportions of 45%, 35%, and 20% respectively. On October 10, 2004, Xumishan Company applied for and obtained the Mining License for the Xumingshan Lead-Zinc Mine of Xumishan Company. Based on the above facts, the defendants' cross-border mining activities constituted a serious infringement upon the lawfully obtained mining rights of Baiyin Company. Therefore, Baiyin Company requested the court to order the four defendants to jointly compensate Baiyin Company for losses of RMB 52,348,500 and bear all litigation costs in this case.

Separately found: On May 21, 2007, the Baiyin Intermediate People's Court of Gansu Province issued civil ruling (2007) Bai Zhong Min Po Zi No. 2 regarding Baiyin Company's bankruptcy application, declaring Baiyin Company bankrupt for liquidation. On November 20, 2007, the court issued civil ruling (2007) Bai Zhong Min Po Zi No. 2-2: "1. The bankruptcy liquidation proceedings for Baiyin Company are terminated: ... 3. The liquidation group shall continue to perform its statutory duties."

During the court trial, Baiyin Company presented the original Mining License, with the mining right holder being Baiyin Company, certificate number 100000982009, and the mine name being Lijiagou Lead-Zinc Mine of Baiyin Nonferrous Metals Company, demonstrating that as of the time of the trial after the conclusion of Baiyin Company's bankruptcy proceedings, no change in the mining right holder had been registered.

On November 24, 2003, Xumishan Company (Party A), Huangzhu Beneficiation Plant (Party B), and No.106 Team (Party C) signed the "Joint Exploration Agreement" stipulating: the exploration rights held by Party B and Party C shall be merged into Party A's exploration rights, and Party A shall conduct exploration within the mining area under the principle of ensuring safety. On October 10, 2004, Xumishan Company applied for and obtained the "Mining License" for the Xumingshan Lead-Zinc Mine of Xumishan Company, license number: 620000410071, valid until October 2012. On June 17, 2005, Xumishan Company and Huangzhu Beneficiation Plant signed the "Agreement on Joint Development of Mineral Resources and Clarification of Responsibilities," stipulating that Huangzhu Beneficiation Plant would independently carry out production and operations and bear all safety responsibilities.

The "Enterprise Legal Person Business License" for Huangzhu Beneficiation Plant, with registration number 6226241003013 issued by the Chengxian County Administration for Industry and Commerce of Gansu Province, indicates that the economic nature of the enterprise is a joint venture. Upon Baiyin Company's application, the original trial court obtained the industrial and commercial registration files of Huangzhu Beneficiation Plant, which proved: Huangzhu Beneficiation Plant was a joint venture enterprise jointly invested by multiple entities including Huangzhu Town Government, Tianshui City Beidao District Mining Development Company, 19 natural persons including Gou Hui, and Longnan Prefectural Party Committee Labor Service Company; on December 1, 2002, Longnan Prefectural Party Committee Labor Service Company received a refund of its joint venture capital contribution of RMB 300,000; on April 28, 2004, the investor Chengxian Huangzhu Town Government signed the "Contract for the Transfer of All Assets of Chengxian Huangzhu Beneficiation Plant (Workshop One)" with Mao Dexian; on March 16, 2004, the investor Tianshui City Beidao District Mining Development Company signed the "Contract for the Transfer of All Assets of Chengxian Huangzhu Beneficiation Plant (Workshop Two)" with Mao Dexian; on April 8, 2004, 19 persons including Gou Hui signed the "Agreement on the Transfer of Individual Shares in Chengxian Huangzhu Town Lead-Zinc Beneficiation Plant" with Mao Dexian. The industrial and commercial files also proved: from the end of 2004 until the cancellation of Huangzhu Beneficiation Plant in 2007, the plant had become a sole proprietorship enterprise owned solely by Mao Dexian. On October 17, 2007, Huangzhu Beneficiation Plant was cancelled, and its claims and debts were not settled. On October 15, 2007, Huangzhu Beneficiation Plant issued a certification to the Chengxian County Administration for Industry and Commerce, stating: "The safety production license, mining license, and pollutant discharge license originally held by the former Chengxian Huangzhu Lead-Zinc Beneficiation Plant are now used by Chengxian Hengxing Mining Co., Ltd."

On October 25, 2007, Hengxing Company was established with registered capital of RMB 11 million. It is a subsidiary company controlled by Gansu Xinyu Mining Co., Ltd., engaged in lead-zinc mining, beneficiation, and sales. Among them: Gansu Xinyu Mining Co., Ltd. contributed RMB 6.6 million, accounting for 60% of the total investment; Mao Dexian contributed RMB 4.4 million, accounting for 40% of the total investment.

The original trial court held that: Based on the parties' claims and defenses as well as the evidence examination opinions during the trial, the disputed issues among the parties are: 1. Whether the litigation subjects of Baiyin Company's liquidation group and Mao Dexian are proper. 2. Whether the four defendants infringed upon the mining rights of Baiyin Company's liquidation group and whether they should bear civil liability. 3. How to bear civil liability and the amount of compensation.

I. Whether the Liquidation Committee of Baiyin Company and Mao Dexian have proper litigation standing. The cross-border mining at issue occurred at the Lijiagou Lead-Zinc Mine of Baiyin Company, where the Mining License lists Baiyin Company as the mining rights holder. On May 21, 2007, the Intermediate People's Court of Baiyin City, Gansu Province, declared Baiyin Company bankrupt for debt repayment by Civil Ruling (2007) Bai Zhong Min Po Zi No. 2, and thereafter lawfully established the Liquidation Committee of Baiyin Company to exercise management rights over the bankrupt enterprise's assets. After the bankruptcy proceedings concluded, the Liquidation Committee was not dissolved and was ordered by the Intermediate People's Court of Baiyin City to continue performing its duties. Therefore, regarding the cross-border mining, the Liquidation Committee of Baiyin Company filed a lawsuit with the People's Court in its own name, which complies with Article 108 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and it has proper standing as a plaintiff. During the original first instance, the plaintiff had provided evidence on this issue, and all defendants acknowledged it. As Defendant No. 106 Team joined this lawsuit after the case was remanded for retrial, after the court explained the matter, Defendant No. 106 Team indicated no objection. Huangzhu Mineral Processing Plant was recorded as a joint venture on its corporate business license, but as of the end of April 2004, all capital contributions from other investors in the Huangzhu Lead-Zinc Mineral Processing Plant had been fully transferred to Mao Dexian personally. When the infringement dispute arose on October 23, 2006, the Huangzhu Mineral Processing Plant was owned solely by Mao Dexian, and after the plant was dissolved, its creditor's rights and debts should be borne by Mao Dexian personally. The Liquidation Committee of Baiyin Company's claim against Mao Dexian is in accordance with the law and is not improper.

II. Whether the four defendants infringed the mining rights of the Liquidation Committee of Baiyin Company and whether they should bear civil liability. During the trial, the four defendants did not dispute the existence of the infringement facts but only raised objections as to whether each should bear civil liability. Xumishan Company and Hengxing Company argued that the illegal mining had already been administratively penalized, and under the principle of "no double jeopardy for the same act," the Liquidation Committee of Baiyin Company had no right to claim civil damages. The court held that "no double jeopardy for the same act" is a fundamental principle of administrative penalty law, meaning that an administrative authority cannot impose two penalties for the same administrative violation. In this case, the Liquidation Committee of Baiyin Company filed a civil tort compensation lawsuit, which is a different legal relationship from administrative penalties. The Land and Resources Bureau of Longnan City imposed an administrative penalty on Xumishan Company in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Mineral Resources Law of the People's Republic of China, but that administrative penalty only represented Xumishan Company's liability for violating administrative law and could not replace other legal liabilities it should bear. At the same time, pursuant to Article 7 of the Administrative Penalty Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides: "If a citizen, legal person, or other organization that has been subjected to administrative penalty for illegal conduct causes damage to others, it shall bear civil liability in accordance with the law," the Liquidation Committee of Baiyin Company's civil tort compensation claim is lawful.

Regarding how the four defendants should bear corresponding civil liability in this case, the facts ascertained at trial show: (1) Huangzhu Mineral Processing Plant, Xumishan Company, and No. 106 Team progressed from joint mineral exploration to joint mining, with each having separate responsibilities and sharing benefits; (2) their respective tasks and work contents within the joint entity differed: Huangzhu Mineral Processing Plant was responsible for mining operations, Xumishan Company provided the mining license, and No. 106 Team used the mine tunnel originally used for exploration as the main haulage roadway for joint mining; (3) the assumption of administrative liability for the illegal acts after the infringement also demonstrates that the three parties had joint intent and agreement to share risks in infringing the mining rights of the Liquidation Committee of Baiyin Company. The party subjected to the administrative penalty was Xumishan Company, but the fine was paid on its behalf by Mao Dexian's arrangement. Therefore, Huangzhu Mineral Processing Plant, Xumishan Company, and No. 106 Team jointly committed the tort; after Huangzhu Mineral Processing Plant was dissolved, its civil liability should be borne jointly by its owner Mao Dexian and Hengxing Company, which succeeded to part of its property.

III. Regarding the amount of compensation. The amount of civil compensation depends on the extent of the infringement losses. The determination of infringement losses in this case focuses on two aspects: first, the confirmation of the quantity of illegally mined ore; second, the confirmation of the price of the illegally mined ore. The court states the findings based on the facts as follows:

Regarding the quantity of illegally mined ore. The loss of 27,288 tons of ore claimed by the Liquidation Committee of Baiyin Company was strictly calculated based on data obtained from on-site measurements of the illegal mining site during the joint investigation team's investigation, using the ore grade and calculation formula determined in the geological report that No. 106 Team submitted to the National Mineral Reserves Committee for review. The data acquisition and calculation method were objective, truthful, and relatively comprehensive. As to whether the measured data is untruthful, as argued by Xumishan Company and Hengxing Company, the following aspects should be considered: after the infringement occurred, Huangzhu Mineral Processing Plant did not preserve the site but instead used multiple blasting and sealing methods to obstruct the investigation of the cross-border mined ore, making it impossible to accurately verify the losses. These circumstances have been confirmed in administrative documents from provincial, municipal, and county governments and mineral resource functional authorities. Moreover, they are reflected and corroborated in digital photos and video footage of the illegal mining site. Even in the No. 1 Prospecting Institute's "Estimation Report," it explicitly states that the 97-line stope could not be entered due to sealing, and it makes no mention of the 105-line III2 stope. In this lawsuit, none of the defendants presented contrary evidence to the court on this issue. Based on the principle of preponderance of evidence and Article 102, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides: "Forging or destroying important evidence to obstruct the People's Court's trial of a case," Huangzhu Mineral Processing Plant should bear the adverse legal consequences of its act of sealing and destroying important evidence through blasting. Second, the grade and calculation formula for lead-zinc ore used by the Liquidation Committee of Baiyin Company in calculating the ore quantity have sufficient basis. The geological report reviewed by the National Ore Reserves Committee is highly authoritative, and moreover, the report's grade and specific gravity calculation formulas for lead-zinc ore were specifically targeted at the No. I and No. III2 ore bodies involved in the case, making them highly relevant; the description of the dip angles of the 105-line III2 ore body and the 97-line I ore body in the report is completely consistent with the dip angles shown in the "97-line Reserve Calculation Profile of Lijiagou Lead-Zinc Deposit" and the "105-line Reserve Calculation Profile of Lijiagou Lead-Zinc Deposit" drawn by No. 106 Team, which was responsible for geological exploration of the Chengxian Lijiagou Lead-Zinc Deposit. The "Estimation Report" submitted by the defendant's No. 1 Prospecting Institute contains only partial ore quantities from one of the three illegal mining stopes, and it is itself incomplete; the direct cause of this incompleteness is the blasting sealing and refusal to clear by Huangzhu Mineral Processing Plant. Huangzhu Mineral Processing Plant and Mao Dexian's signing and sealing on the cross-border mining plan is the best illustration of this issue.

Regarding the price of lead concentrate and zinc concentrate. The defendants argued that compensation should not be based on market prices. The Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China provides relatively clear provisions on this point, i.e., for infringement of property rights, compensation is based on the market price of the infringed property. The explanation given by the Liquidation Committee of Baiyin Company regarding the purchase prices of lead concentrate and zinc concentrate is reasonable. The invoices for lead concentrate and zinc concentrate submitted by the Liquidation Committee of Baiyin Company are all market transaction prices with third parties in October 1996, which were the market prices at the time the infringement occurred. The calculation method was to add the four unit prices for lead concentrate and zinc concentrate separately and then divide the total price by four to obtain the average market price at that time, which is consistent with the principle of the Tort Liability Law that losses from infringement of property rights are calculated based on the market price of the infringed property at the time of infringement. In summary, in accordance with Articles 117 and 130 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, the court ruled: Mao Dexian, Xumishan Company, and No. 106 Team shall jointly and severally compensate the Liquidation Committee of Baiyin Company in the amount of RMB 52,348,500 within ten days after the judgment takes effect. Hengxing Company shall bear supplementary compensation liability for the portion of compensation borne by Mao Dexian, limited to the assets of Huangzhu Mineral Processing Plant that it succeeded. The case acceptance fee of RMB 303,543 shall be borne by Mao Dexian in the amount of RMB 103,543, by Xumishan Company in the amount of RMB 100,000, and by Hengxing Company in the amount of RMB 100,000.

Mao Dexian, Xumishan Company, No. 106 Team, and Hengxing Company all disagreed with the above civil judgment of the original trial court and appealed to this court. Mao Dexian appealed, arguing: The original judgment found unclear facts and misapplied the law; he requested that the above civil judgment of the original trial court be reversed and the case be retried in accordance with the law; and that the litigation costs be borne by the Liquidation Committee of Baiyin Company. The main reasons are: 1. The original judgment found unclear facts and insufficient evidence. (1) The original judgment's finding that "the three illegal mining stopes involved in this case" was erroneous. The Land and Resources Bureau of Longnan City and the Department of Land and Resources of Gansu Province characterized the "10.23" incident in their reports as "cross-border mining" rather than "illegal mining"; the mining locations were also not as described. Even if the administrative authority's characterization of the incident and the identification of the stopes involved were wrong, before the lawful revocation through statutory procedures, no organ or administrative counterpart may arbitrarily alter their content. (2) The original judgment's finding that "during the investigation period, the investigation team commissioned the Appellee's Bankruptcy Liquidation Committee of Baiyin Nonferrous Metals Company to conduct on-site measurements of the stopes" was erroneous. The Liquidation Committee of Baiyin Company conducted the on-site measurements on October 23, 2006, which was before the establishment of the municipal-level investigation team, and even before the establishment of the provincial, municipal, and county joint investigation team. Since the investigation team had not yet been established, there could be no "investigation period"; there were no entrustment procedures or records from the investigation team in this case, and the appellant was not given the opportunity to cross-examine the evidence materials concerning this entrusted investigation. (3) The original judgment's assertion that the No. 1 Prospecting Institute's "Estimation Report" was subjectively divided into "the 105-line stope part" had no factual basis; the No. 1 Prospecting Institute, as an independent legal entity qualified for mineral resource reserve evaluation, estimated the mineral resource reserves of the 105-line stope and the 97-line stope, and the "Estimation Report" had been confirmed by the mineral resource authority, making it lawful and objectively truthful; if the original judgment considered the "Estimation Report" insufficient to determine the facts of the case, it should have lawfully referred the matter to a statutory appraisal institution for supplementary appraisal or reappraisal, rather than exceeding its authority to directly determine its probative value. (4) The appellant and Huangzhu Mineral Processing Plant's signing and sealing on the "Cross-Border Mining Investigation Plan" and the official seal of Huangzhu Mineral Processing Plant have no relevance to the facts found by the original judgment; the Liquidation Committee of Baiyin Company and Xumishan Company were clearing their own mining tunnels over which they held mining rights, which does not prove that the appellant and Huangzhu Mineral Processing Plant carried out the blasting sealing actions; the existence of abandoned civilian mining tunnels within the mining rights area of the Liquidation Committee of Baiyin Company was not caused by cross-border mining. (5) The "Mineral Resources Administrative Penalty Decision" of the Land and Resources Bureau of Longnan City is a specific administrative act by the national mining administrative authority, with legal credibility and enforceability; until lawfully revoked through statutory procedures, it constitutes the final determination of the ore unit price, total ore quantity, and total illegal gains in the cross-border mining incident; although this administrative penalty and the civil tort compensation lawsuit in this case are different legal relationships, this penalty decision is the result of the national mineral resource administrative authority applying the law based on ascertaining objective facts, is an important piece of evidence regarding the basic facts of the case, and does not conflict with the civil tort legal relationship. (6) Regarding the determination of the compensation amount. The "On-Site Measurement Materials" made by the Liquidation Committee of Baiyin Company are only party statements; the Liquidation Committee itself does not have the qualification to evaluate mineral resource reserves and cannot be used as a basis for determining case facts; the original judgment found that the invoice prices for lead concentrate and zinc concentrate submitted by the Liquidation Committee of Baiyin Company conform to the spirit of the law regarding market prices at the relevant time, but the original judgment did not consider factors such as mining costs, management costs, sales costs, resource taxes and fees, quantities of surrounding rock and waste rock, local beneficiation levels, recovery rates, etc.; the calculated compensation amount lacks an objective and truthful factual basis and violates the basic spirit of "compensating actual damages" under the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. 2. The original judgment improperly applied the law. The newly established Hengxing Company succeeded to and accepted all high-quality assets of the former Huangzhu Lead-Zinc Mineral Processing Plant, and there were no changes in the company's domicile, legal representative, business scope, or business operations; Hengxing Company continued production and business activities based on the original asset foundation of Huangzhu Lead-Zinc Mineral Processing Plant, following the original established business objectives, and naturally became the successor of the rights and obligations of Huangzhu Lead-Zinc Mineral Processing Plant; accordingly, Mao Dexian personally cannot be considered a proper subject for bearing the debts after the dissolution of Huangzhu Mineral Processing Plant. The original judgment's finding that Huangzhu Mineral Processing Plant carried out blasting sealing and refused to clear was an unlawful presumption without legal basis.

Xumishan Company appealed, arguing: The original judgment found unclear facts and insufficient evidence; it requested that the judgment be reversed and the case be retried. The main reasons are: 1. The quantity of cross-border mined ore and the losses should be determined either by a qualified third-party professional institution's appraisal and evaluation, or by a joint investigation team verifying and confirming the on-site measurement results of the Liquidation Committee of Baiyin Company. The first-instance court, without verification, excluded the probative value of the company's submitted public documentary evidence, such as the three-level investigation team of the Department of Land and Resources of Gansu Province's "Request for Instructions on the Investigation and Handling Opinion of the '10.23' Cross-Border Mining Incident" and the "Administrative Penalty Decision," and determined the facts of the case, including the quantity of cross-border mined ore, based solely on Baiyin Company's unilateral on-site measurement materials. This has no legal basis and violates the Civil Procedure Law. The "Estimation Report" issued by the No. 1 Prospecting Institute, commissioned by the joint investigation team on November 25, 2006, is truthful and reliable. 2. The first-instance judgment incorrectly applied the law and was manifestly unfair. The first-instance court's ruling that Huangzhu Mineral Processing Plant should bear the adverse legal consequences of its act of blasting sealing and destroying important evidence was a misapplication of the law and a clear favoritism toward Baiyin Company. The first-instance judgment's application of the Tort Liability Law to order the infringer to compensate based on the market price of the infringed property was a misapplication resulting from a misunderstanding of the law. In calculating compensation, the costs and expenses and taxes that would have necessarily been incurred by Baiyin Company had it mined the ore itself, as well as those incurred as a result of cross-border mining, should be deducted from the product sales price under the principle of offsetting profits and losses. When Baiyin Company calculated the loss amount, using the self-measured cross-border mining quantity and the theoretical grade from the geological reserve report to calculate the lead and zinc metal content, this was actually only a theoretical figure, not the actual producible output in industrial production. The Tort Liability Law does not have retroactive effect in judicial practice.

106 Team appealed, stating: It requested the court of second instance to legally vacate the original judgment, amend the judgment or remand the case for retrial according to law; and to rule that the appellant's costs in this case be borne by Baiyin Company's liquidation group. The main reasons were: 1. Team 106 was not the subject of tort liability in this case. The judgment of first instance found that Team 106 was a joint tortfeasor in this case, but the evidence was clearly insufficient. (a) The "Joint Prospecting Agreement" signed on November 24, 2003, covered cooperation matters for prospecting within the area where it held lawful prospecting rights. Pursuant to that agreement, Team 106 had confirmed that its prospecting rights belonged to Xumishan Company, and the specific prospecting work was independently carried out by that company, with Team 106 no longer participating. From the content of that agreement, it could not be proven that Team 106 had any intention to engage in joint "mining" with others or to "jointly commit infringing acts" related thereto. Although Team 106 established a legal relationship for joint prospecting with Xumishan Company and Huangzhu Ore Dressing Plant in 2003, it submitted a reconnaissance report to the competent authority in May 2004, ending the prospecting work. When Xumishan Company lawfully obtained the mining right for Xumingshan in October 2004, the joint prospecting relationship within the mining right area had already terminated. The finding in the investigation report of the Longnan Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources that "from this point onward, the three-party joint prospecting turned into joint mining" had no valid evidentiary support. Even so, the legal relationship for three-party joint mining, because there existed a lawful mining right (the Xumingshan mining right), was a lawful and valid legal relationship. (b) The judgment of first instance found that Team 106 had used the mine adit originally used for prospecting as the main transport passage for joint mining. This finding was erroneous and lacked factual basis. Team 106 never intended to deliver the prospecting mine adit involved to any third party for lawful or unlawful use; after the prospecting work ended, Team 106 had no legal duty to continue managing or guarding the prospecting mine adit. After repeated investigations and findings by the competent authorities at the provincial (Gansu) and municipal (Longnan) levels, the infringer in this case of cross-border mining was Xumishan Company, which had borne the corresponding administrative liability. Team 106 was not found to have constituted joint infringement. 2. As to the calculation of property loss, i.e., the consequence of the tort damage in this case, the judgment of first instance contained errors of a certain degree, which seriously increased the burden on the infringer. (a) As to the quantity of infringing ore: According to the joint investigation results of three levels of government departments in Gansu Province and the "Administrative Penalty Decision for Mineral Resources" issued by the Longnan Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources, the quantity of infringing ore should be 4,907 tons, including 2,005 tons from ore body III2, line 109. However, the court of first instance, based solely on Baiyin Company's unilateral survey results, determined the quantity of infringing ore as 27,288 tons. The error is evident. The quantity of infringing ore confirmed in the "Estimation Report" of the First Geological Exploration Institute also proved the objectivity, scientific basis, and fairness of the basis used by the three levels of government departments in determining the quantity of infringing ore. (b) As to the grade of infringing ore: The court of first instance used the ore grade (lead 1.29%, zinc 8%) shown in the "Geological Exploration Report of the Lijia Gully Lead-Zinc Deposit in Cheng County, Gansu Province" submitted by Baiyin Company to calculate the quantity of lead concentrate and zinc concentrate. This was improper admission of evidence, and the result was erroneous. That exploration report was prepared in March 1986. At that time, the exploration technology and equipment were clearly inferior to those in 2009, so its precision and error margin were naturally larger. In comparison, the data determined in the "Estimation Report" prepared by the First Geological Exploration Institute after the infringement incident occurred in 2006, and the "Verification Report on Resource Reserves of the Lijia Gully Lead-Zinc Deposit in Cheng County, Gansu Province" prepared by the Second Geological Exploration Institute of the Gansu Provincial Bureau of Geology and Mineral Exploration and Development commissioned by Baiyin Company in November 2009, and the review opinions, were more scientific and accurate and should have been admitted. (c) As to the market price basis for the infringed property: The infringing act occurred in October 2006. If Baiyin Company provided sales invoices from 1996, how could they be recognized as "market prices at the time of the infringing act"? The VAT invoices submitted by Baiyin Company for court cross-examination consisted of 5 for zinc concentrate and 2 for lead concentrate, totaling 7 invoices. How could they be recognized as "the current market average price obtained by adding the four unit prices for lead concentrate and zinc concentrate respectively and then dividing the total by four"? The price should be determined by comprehensively considering the sales prices provided by the appellant, sales prices provided by unrelated parties, and the government's statistical prices for the period in Gansu Province, which would be more objective and fair. Some of the invoices submitted by Baiyin Company were suspected of being related-party transactions and should not have been used as the basis for the case. Since the judgment of first instance held that "the loss from infringement of property rights shall be calculated based on the current market average price of the infringed property," the infringer infringed Baiyin Company's mining right to the mineral resources involved. Therefore, the calculation should be based on the market average price of the mining right to the mineral resources that the infringer had already infringed, not the market average price of lead concentrate and zinc concentrate. The loss should be determined by assessing the transfer price of the mining right for the infringed mine and establishing the loss based on the assessment results, which would comply with the spirit of tort liability law. (d) As to the calculation of loss from property infringement: The legislative intent of Article 19 of the Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China is to use the "market price at the time of the loss occurrence" as the specific calculation basis, while also considering relevant factors and making a comprehensive determination, rather than directly applying that price. According to the "Guidelines for Mining Right Assessment" and the theoretical and practical common knowledge of many stages such as mine mining and beneficiation, because the infringer infringed upon lead-zinc mine resources, and mineral resources can only be ultimately converted into lead concentrate and zinc concentrate after mining, beneficiation, transportation, and management, if the loss of lead-zinc mine resources is directly calculated based on lead concentrate and zinc concentrate, then costs and expenses such as mining costs, beneficiation costs, mining losses, beneficiation losses, management fees, transportation fees, etc., which even the appellee would have to bear if it mined itself, would undoubtedly be imposed on the infringer as losses, which is necessarily erroneous. The Gansu High People's Court correctly analyzed and affirmed this view in its civil judgment (2008) Gan Min Er Chu Zi No. 15.

Hengxing Company appealed, stating: The judgment of first instance had unclear facts, insufficient evidence, and erroneous application of law. It requested that the judgment be vacated and amended according to law. The main reasons were: 1. The quantity of cross-border mined ore and the loss should be determined by a qualified third-party professional institution through appraisal and assessment, or confirmed by the joint investigation team after checking and verifying the appellee's actual survey results. The court of first instance, relying solely on Baiyin Company's unilateral survey data, determined the quantity of cross-border mining without legal basis. That survey data contradicted the situation reflected in Li Kuang Zi [2006] No. 18 and the investigation conclusions of the administrative authorities at the provincial and municipal levels. The "Estimation Report" issued by the First Geological Exploration Institute on November 25, 2006, commissioned by the joint investigation team, was truthful and reliable. 2. The judgment of first instance erred in applying the law, and the judgment was manifestly unfair. The judgment of first instance held that Huangzhu Ore Dressing Plant should bear adverse legal consequences for its act of sealing off the passage with explosives and destroying important evidence. This was an erroneous application of the law and a clear favoritism toward Baiyin Company. Official documentary evidence such as the "Request for Instructions on the Handling Opinions on the '10-23' Cross-Border Mining Incident in the Lijia Gully Lead-Zinc Mining Area of Baiyin Company, Cheng County" from the Department of Land and Resources of Gansu Province and other documents from administrative authorities and on-site assessment reports from professional institutions should have greater probative value than the indirect evidence such as general documentary evidence lacking authenticity requirements, drawings, photographs, and video materials submitted by the appellee. The judgment of first instance applied the Tort Liability Law to order the infringer to compensate based on the market price of the infringed property. This was an erroneous application of law resulting from a misunderstanding of the law. The infringement act in this case occurred in 2006. The Tort Liability Law has no retroactive effect on the infringement act in this case. Civil liability should be determined in accordance with the compensation liability form of compensation by equivalent value as stipulated in Article 117 of the General Principles of the Civil Law. In this case, Baiyin Company's loss should be equivalent to the net profit it could have obtained if it had itself mined, processed, and sold the same quantity of ore that was cross-border mined, not the total sales revenue.

Baiyin Company jointly responded to the appeals of the four appellants, stating: The judgment of first instance had clear findings of fact, correct application of law, and lawful admission of evidence, and should be upheld. The stopes involved in the cross-border mining in this case were three, not two as allegedly claimed by the appellants, as evidenced by the report of the Longnan Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources and Baiyin Company's survey report. Baiyin Company's survey report was made at the request of the Longnan Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources and the Gansu Provincial Department of Land and Resources for Baiyin Company to participate in the administrative penalty investigation and assist the investigation team. The report and attached drawings are archived in the relevant files of the Longnan Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources, with signatures and seals of Mao Dexian and Huangzhu Ore Dressing Plant on the relevant attached drawings. The court's admission was lawful and proper. As to the calculation of ore quantity, if converted to run-of-mine ore, the cost would be higher. Baiyin Company's calculation was made using the formula prescribed by the state. The recovery rate, grade, etc., had already excluded waste ore, and corresponding calculations were made. As to the issue of subject status, all four appellants met the status of defendants and should bear civil liability according to law.

In addition to confirming the facts found by the court of first instance, this court further finds: 1. The "Investigation Report on the '10-23' Illegal Cross-Border Mining Situation in the Lijia Gully Mining Area, Cheng County" submitted by the Longnan Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources to the Longnan Municipal People's Government on November 2, 2006 (Long Guo Tu Zi Bao [2006] No. 71) stated: In accordance with the instructions of the municipal government leadership and based on the "Urgent Report on '10-23' Illegal Cross-Border Mining" from Cheng County Lijia Gully Mining Co., Ltd., our bureau formed a joint investigation team. The investigation was conducted from October 28 to October 30 and revealed that Huangzhu Ore Dressing Plant had applied for and obtained the "Exploration License" for the general survey project of the Ciba South Lead-Zinc Mine in Cheng County, Gansu, valid from December 28, 2001 to December 28, 2003. On November 24, 2003, Xumishan Company, Huangzhu Ore Dressing Plant, and Team 106 signed the "Joint Prospecting Agreement," with their respective prospecting proportions being 45%, 35%, and 20%. On October 10, 2004, Xumishan Company applied for and obtained the "Mining License" for Xumishan Company's Xumingshan Lead-Zinc Mine, valid until October 2012. At that point, the three-party joint prospecting became joint mining. During the prospecting phase, a joint monitoring agreement was signed with Changba Lead-Zinc Mine, resulting in the original Team 106 prospecting tunnel at the Xumingshan Mine (Qijiagou mine adit) being used as the main transport roadway. Upon inspection and investigation, the problem of "10-23" illegal cross-border mining reported by Lijia Gully Mine existed, and the basic situation was consistent. Due to the failure to promptly take effective measures to protect the scene and promptly order the cessation of all mining activities and the sealing or blocking of the Xumingshan Mine Qijiagou mine adit (the original Team 106 prospecting tunnel), this investigation could not conduct technical monitoring or accurately verify and define the scope of the mined-out area. 2. The "Request for Instructions on the Handling Opinions on the '10-23' Cross-Border Mining Incident in the Lijia Gully Lead-Zinc Mining Area of Baiyin Company, Cheng County" submitted by the Gansu Provincial Department of Land and Resources to the Gansu Provincial People's Government on February 13, 2007 (Gan Guo Tu Zi Fa [2007] No. 31) stated: In accordance with Governor Xu Shousheng's instructions, the Provincial Department of Land and Resources, together with the Provincial Administration of Work Safety, the Longnan Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources, the Longnan Municipal Administration of Work Safety, the Cheng County Government, the Cheng County Bureau of Land and Resources, Baiyin Company, and other relevant units, formed a joint investigation team. The investigation was conducted from November 23 to November 30 regarding the "10-23" cross-border mining situation. The joint investigation team heard the introduction of the cross-border mining situation from Baiyin Company's Lijia Gully Lead-Zinc Mine, carefully reviewed the relevant materials of the Lijia Gully Lead-Zinc Mine and Xumishan Company's Xumingshan Lead-Zinc Mine, and found that the subject of the cross-border mining was Xumishan Company's Xumingshan Lead-Zinc Mine. The cross-border mining area was in the area from line 102 to line 109 of ore body III2 and around line 97 of ore body I, which was basically consistent with the situation reported by Baiyin Company. The joint investigation team commissioned the First Geological Exploration Institute to calculate the quantity of ore mined in the cross-border area. The calculated mining quantity near the stope near line 109 was approximately 2,005 tons. The stope near line 97 could not be accurately calculated because the mining tunnel had been sealed and could not be entered. This cross-border mining occurred in the 1155-meter level, which actually utilized the original Team 106 prospecting tunnel at the entrance of Qijiagou, owned by the Nonferrous Geological Exploration Bureau. 3. The Gansu Provincial Department of Land and Resources led the formation of a three-level joint investigation team to investigate the cross-border mining incident involved. Baiyin Company was a member of the investigation team. The main responsibilities of the investigation team were: (1) To conduct mining engineering surveys of Xumishan Company's Xumingshan Lead-Zinc Mine; (2) To conduct technical appraisal of the quantity of mined ore; (3) To submit a technical monitoring investigation report. 4. On October 11, 1999, Team 106 and Huangzhu Ore Dressing Plant signed the "Joint Prospecting Contract for the Ciba Lead-Zinc Mine in Cheng County, Gansu Province," stipulating: Huangzhu Ore Dressing Plant held 70% of the prospecting rights, and Team 106 held 30% of the prospecting rights; Team 106 was responsible for the technical and management work during prospecting, drafting prospecting designs, submitting them to the Gansu Nonferrous Geological Exploration Bureau for approval before implementation, and providing the necessary professional and technical personnel, and strictly constructing in accordance with the design requirements and specifications; the ore recovered during prospecting, and the ore mined after application for a combination of prospecting and mining and after application for formal mining, were to be distributed according to the above prospecting rights proportion. 5. On January 18, 2001, Huangzhu Ore Dressing Plant and Team 106 signed the "Cooperative Detailed Survey Contract for the East Lead-Zinc Mine, Peripheral to the Changba-Lijia Gully Lead-Zinc Deposit in Cheng County, Gansu Province," stipulating: The parties, based on their previous joint prospecting, were willing to continue joint risk prospecting. When conditions for development were met, the parties would continue joint development until the mine was closed due to depletion. The remaining content of the contract concluded on October 11, 1999, between the above parties was reaffirmed in this contract. 6. On April 23, 2002, Team 106, Huangzhu Ore Dressing Plant, and Cheng County Ciba Concentrator Xumishan Mine signed the "Joint Prospecting Agreement," stipulating: The mining certificate held by Cheng County Ciba Concentrator Xumishan Mine, within the prospecting areas of the other two parties, was willing to invest funds for further prospecting, obtaining joint prospecting rights, with the joint prospecting rights unit being Xumishan Company. The prospecting work was designed by Team 106 and organized and constructed by Cheng County Ciba Concentrator Xumishan Mine. After the agreement took effect, Team 106 and Huangzhu Ore Dressing Plant provided relevant preliminary geological data; Team 106 was responsible for providing geological prospecting tunnel surveying and geological data, etc., and monitoring once every two to three months; during the implementation and operation of the joint prospecting, the joint venture parties, Huangzhu Ore Dressing Plant and Team 106, each sent one ore supervisor to carry out supervision work; within the area of the two mines, if mutual entry occurred after prospecting and mining intersected, priority was given to the Huangzhu Ore Dressing Plant tunnel, and Team 106's tunnel would proactively detour to continue prospecting and mining activities. 7. The "Joint Prospecting Agreement" signed on November 24, 2003, by Xumishan Company, Huangzhu Ore Dressing Plant, and Team 106 stated: The three parties agreed to merge the prospecting certificates of Xumishan Company, Huangzhu Ore Dressing Plant, and Team 106 and change them to Xumishan Company's prospecting rights, implementing unified planning and unified management. This joint prospecting agreement was signed specially: The three parties agreed to merge the above two prospecting rights under the name of Xumishan Company, with the three parties jointly funding and conducting exploration and development according to law; the three parties agreed to invest certain funds for joint exploration, with the three parties' respective prospecting proportions being: Xumishan Company 45%, Huangzhu Ore Dressing Plant 35%, and Team 106 20%; Xumishan Company organized construction management, and Team 106, as a qualified geological exploration unit, implemented geological exploration work within the new joint prospecting rights area. The joint company was to be managed in accordance with the "Company Law." 8. During the trial of the second instance, Team 106 acknowledged that the parties had distributed recovered and mined ore several times in accordance with the proportions agreed in the above several agreements. 9. In the judgment of first instance, page 26, paragraph 2, line 5, the phrase "the invoices for lead concentrate and zinc concentrate were the market transaction prices with unrelated parties in October 1996" was a clerical error; the year should be October 2006.

This court, after trial, finds that, according to the parties' appeal and response opinions, the issues in dispute in the second instance of this case are: 1. Whether Mao Dexian and Team 106 should be defendants in this case. 2. How the amount of tort loss in this case should be determined. 3. How the four appellants should bear civil liability in this case.

关于茅德贤与106队应否成为本案被告问题。黄渚选矿厂系涉案联合探矿协议的签约主体之一，亦为“10·23”越界开采的实际操作主体，该厂作为联营企业至2004年4月，其全部出资已由茅德贤个人受让；该厂虽已被当地工商部门注销，但该厂未就其债权债务予以清算，故茅德贤应依法对黄渚选矿厂的债权债务承担民事责任。白银公司向茅德贤主张权利，并要求其承担侵权责任，符合我国民事诉讼法及民法通则的规定，原审判决将茅德贤列为本案被告，并无不当，本院予以维持。本案一、二审查明的事实表明，自1999年10月至2003年11月，黄渚选矿厂、106队与须弥山公司签订数份联合探矿合同与合作勘查合同，合同约定各方联合探矿、探采结合、逐步转入正规开采，直至开采闭坑为止；约定106队负责技术及管理工作，提供技术资料；对三方各自所占探矿比例、矿石回收分配比例等均作出了相应约定，且三方认可实际已依约履行。陇南市国土资源局的相关调查报告亦认定三方由联合探矿变为联合采矿，而本次越界开采的主运输巷道系106队原探矿巷道。可见，没有106队将自己的探矿权合并到须弥山公司名下，并将自己有权使用的原有探矿巷道作为此次非法越界开采的主运输巷道，供须弥山公司与黄渚选矿厂实际使用，没有106队多年的技术支持，就不会有本案非法越界开采后果的发生。因此，原审判决将106队列为本案被告，同样符合我国民事诉讼法第一百零八条的规定。茅德贤与106队关于自己不应成为本案被告的上诉请求不能成立，本院不予支持。关于本案侵权损失数额的确定问题。从本案查明的事实看，关于涉案“10·23”越界开采事件，陇南市国土资源局与甘肃省国土资源厅已分别组织调查组进行了调查，并分别作出了《陇南市国土资源局关于成县李家沟矿区“10·23”非法越界开采情况的调查报告》与《甘肃省国土资源厅关于白银公司成县李家沟铅锌矿区“10·23”越界开采事件处理意见的请示》，陇南市国土资源局还作出了《矿产资源行政处罚决定书》，就该事件作出了基本结论与处理。当地政府均表态该事件为非法越界开采国有矿藏，事件严重情况与白银公司李家沟铅锌矿反映的情况基本一致；一、二审中，各方当事人对本案侵权事实的存在均予认可。因此，本案作为侵权损害赔偿纠纷，侵权事实客观存在，其与陇南市国土资源局就该事件作出行政处罚，属于民事与行政两个不同性质的法律关系，二者在认定事实、适用法律政策方面的依据均有所不同。《中华人民共和国行政处罚法》第七条明确规定“公民、法人或者其他组织因违法受到行政处罚，其违法行为对他人造成损害的，应当依法承担民事责任”，四方上诉人要求按照陇南市国土资源局作出的《矿产资源行政处罚决定书》确认本案民事责任，缺乏法律依据，本院不予支持。

On the issue of whether Mao Dexian and Team 106 should be defendants in this case. The Huangzhu Ore Dressing Plant was one of the signing parties to the joint exploration agreement involved in the case and was also the actual operator of the "10·23" cross-boundary mining. As a joint venture, by April 2004, all of the plant's capital contributions had been individually transferred to Mao Dexian; although the plant has been deregistered by the local industrial and commercial authorities, it did not liquidate its claims and debts, so Mao Dexian should, in accordance with law, bear civil liability for the claims and debts of the Huangzhu Ore Dressing Plant. Baiyin Company asserted its rights against Mao Dexian and requested that he assume tort liability, which complies with the provisions of China's Civil Procedure Law and the General Principles of the Civil Law. The judgment of the first instance listing Mao Dexian as a defendant in this case was not improper, and this Court affirms it. The facts ascertained in the first and second instances of this case show that from October 1999 to November 2003, the Huangzhu Ore Dressing Plant, Team 106, and Xumishan Company entered into several joint exploration contracts and cooperative exploration contracts. The contracts stipulated that the parties would jointly explore, combine exploration with mining, gradually transition to regular mining, and continue until the mine was closed and depleted; and that Team 106 would be responsible for technical and management work and provide technical data. The contracts also made corresponding provisions on the proportions of exploration and ore recovery and distribution among the three parties, and the parties confirmed that they had actually performed the contracts as agreed. The relevant investigation report of the Longnan Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources also determined that the three parties had changed from joint exploration to joint mining, and the main transport roadway for this cross-boundary mining was originally a prospecting roadway of Team 106. It is evident that, without Team 106 merging its prospecting right under Xumishan Company's name and providing the original prospecting roadway it was entitled to use as the main transport roadway for this illegal cross-boundary mining for the actual use of Xumishan Company and the Huangzhu Ore Dressing Plant, and without years of technical support from Team 106, the consequences of the illegal cross-boundary mining in this case would not have occurred. Therefore, the judgment of the first instance listing Team 106 as a defendant in this case also complies with Article 108 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC. The appeals of Mao Dexian and Team 106 that they should not be defendants in this case are untenable, and this Court does not support them.

On the issue of the determination of the amount of tort damages in this case. From the facts ascertained in this case, concerning the "10·23" cross-boundary mining incident involved, the Longnan Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources and the Gansu Provincial Department of Land and Resources each organized investigation teams to conduct investigations and respectively produced the "Investigation Report of the Longnan Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources on the '10·23' Illegal Cross-Boundary Mining Situation in the Lijia Valley Mining Area of Cheng County" and the "Request for Instructions of the Gansu Provincial Department of Land and Resources on the Handling Opinion Regarding the '10·23' Cross-Boundary Mining Incident in the Lijia Valley Lead-Zinc Mining Area of Baiyin Company, Cheng County". The Longnan Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources also issued an "Administrative Penalty Decision on Mineral Resources", making basic conclusions and handling regarding the incident. The local government stated that the incident was an illegal cross-boundary mining of state-owned mineral deposits, and the seriousness of the incident was basically consistent with the situation reported by Baiyin Company's Lijia Valley Lead-Zinc Mine. In the first and second instances, all parties acknowledged the existence of the tortious facts in this case. Therefore, in this case, which is a dispute over tort damages, the tortious facts objectively exist. The administrative penalty imposed by the Longnan Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources regarding the incident constitutes two different legal relationships of civil and administrative natures, with different bases for determining facts and applying laws and policies. Article 7 of the Administrative Penalty Law of the PRC clearly provides: "If a citizen, legal person, or other organization is subject to an administrative penalty for an illegal act, and the illegal act causes damage to others, it shall bear civil liability in accordance with law." The four appellants' request to confirm the civil liability in this case in accordance with the "Administrative Penalty Decision on Mineral Resources" issued by the Longnan Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources lacks legal basis, and this Court does not support it.

关于侵权损失赔偿数额，包括越界采矿数量与矿石损失单价的确认，以及应否剔除越界开采成本问题。一审中，白银公司为支持自己的主张向法庭提供了一系列证据材料，包括参与当地政府调查期间形成的实测资料报告、采场水平平面图、增值税专业发票等，经过一审法庭质证，有关当事人对其真实性或者表示认可，或者虽提出异议，但并未提出相应的反驳证据。本院二审中，原审四被告均提出上诉，认为原审判决在证据的认定与采纳方面不符合我国法律要求，经本院释明后，各方仍均未提出相应有效的合法证据予以反驳。根据本院《关于民事诉讼证据的若干规定》第二条“当事人对自己提出的诉讼请求所依据的事实或反驳对方诉讼请求所依据的事实有责任提供证据加以证明。没有证据或者证据不足以证明当事人的事实主张的，由负有举证责任的当事人承担不利后果”之规定，四方上诉人应当承担举证不能的法律责任。首先，白银公司主张的27288吨矿石损失数量问题，该数量系地方政府两次组织调查前后，白银公司清算组作为联合调查组成员对越界开采现场实际测量取得数据，再依据国家矿产储量委员会审核通过的106队作出的相关地质报告所确定的矿石品位及计算公式严格计算出来的；且包括该数据在内的有关越界开采的事实情况报告得到了陇南市国土资源局以及甘肃省国土资源厅三级联合调查组的肯定，并成为陇南市国土资源局作出行政处罚的基本依据之一，具有相当的权威性。该数据系理论计算结果，本应通过实地核查予以印证，但由于黄渚选矿厂在越界开采行为被发现后，不但没有停止侵权、保护现场，反而多次实施爆破、封堵等恶意阻挠行为，陇南市国土资源局多次发文责令其停止侵权行为并立即清理，但黄渚选矿厂拒不清理，阻挠有关调查，致使矿产损失至今无法准确核实。该爆破、封堵行为是本案侵权行为的延续和实际损失不能准确核查的主要原因，已被地方与矿产资源管理机构的有效行政文件所确认。在地方政府组织的调查组对该越界开采事件调查处理过程中，茅德贤与黄渚选矿厂在该调查组成员白银公司清算组出具的“越界开采调查平面图”上签字、加盖公章，对自己实施的侵权行为以及该行为实施的范围、位置予以认可。而在本案诉讼中，茅德贤又拒绝承认黄渚选矿厂实施了爆堵行为，否认该厂越界开采行为与损害后果之间的关联性，有违诚实信用原则，据此，本院不予支持。至于一勘院基于甘肃省国土资源厅三级联合调查组委托就侵权事实所作的《估算报告》亦明确97线采场因为封堵无法进入，但该报告对105线Ⅲ2采场未提及，一些损失计算所必要的数据未提供，原审法院对该《估算报告》未予采纳，符合我国民事诉讼证据规则的规定，并无不妥。本院二审中，106队向本院提出申请，请求由权威部门就本案侵权产生的矿石损失予以鉴定。对此，本院认为，基于本案业已查明的案件事实，已不可能恢复越界开采当时的历史原貌，本案已不存在进行相关鉴定的条件，故本院不予准许。原审判决认定本案越界开采矿石数量为27288吨，并以国家矿产储量委员会1988年1月审批的106队呈报的《甘肃省成县李家沟铅锌矿床地质勘探报告》所确定的矿石品位及计算公式计算本案侵权损失数额，符合我国民事诉讼证据规则的基本要求，并无不妥，本院予以维持。其次，四方上诉人在上诉意见中均提出在计算损失具体数额时应当采用原矿价格而非精粉价格。本院在二审期间依职权走访咨询了国土资源部、陇南市国土资源局与物价局等部门，均无法查询到确切的涉案原矿石的市场价格或者国家指导性价格等直接证据；如前所述，由于上诉人方面的原因，采场已无法恢复原状，本案已不具备法定的鉴定条件，上诉人又未提出有效的合法证据加以反驳，依照证据规则要求，上诉人应当承担举证不能的法律后果。故原审判决实际采纳白银公司2006年（非1996年）10月即越界开采被发现当月购买铅精粉和锌精粉价格发票的平均值，符合本院民事诉讼证据规则的要求，本院予以维持。对于上诉人提出的计算损失具体数额时应剔除开采、选矿成本与损失、支出的管理运输费用、税费等问题。本院认为，本案系侵犯采矿权纠纷，本案中的越界开采行为系非法侵权行为，不同于一般的合法商业交易行为。该非法行为持续多年，使国有矿山资源遭受巨大破坏，造成国有资产的流失，严重损害了国家利益；在该侵权行为被发现、相关国家管理部门三令五申立即停止侵权的情况下，侵权人仍通过爆破、封堵等手段阻挠调查，毁灭证据，已被国家有关部门予以行政处罚，故对这种恶意侵权行为人民法院应当进行制裁。原矿石被开采出来后经过加工、运输等生产程序，转换成精粉等深加工产品，在计算侵权损失时扣除开采、运输、人工工资、税收等必要的成本，得出净利润予以赔偿，是一般正常合同交易损害赔偿纠纷中通常使用的计算方法。本案当事人的侵权行为完全不同于一般矿石开采交易，而是恶意侵犯国有资产，性质严重，造成的国有资产损失难以估量，将如此恶意侵权行为所付出的成本由受害方国有企业承担，既无法律依据，亦不合情理。且上诉人在一审反驳、二审上诉中经法院释明后均拒绝提供自己非法越界开采成本的相关证据，故本院对此不予支持。因此，上诉人关于重新确认价格和损失的上诉请求缺乏事实和法律依据，不能成立，本院不予支持。

Regarding the amount of compensation for tort losses, including the determination of the quantity of cross-boundary mined ore and the unit price of ore loss, and whether the cost of cross-boundary mining should be deducted. In the first instance, Baiyin Company submitted a series of evidentiary materials to the court in support of its claims, including a measured data report formed during its participation in the local government's investigation, horizontal plan views of the stope, and special value-added tax invoices. After cross-examination at the first instance, the relevant parties either acknowledged the authenticity of these materials or, although raising objections, did not provide corresponding rebuttal evidence. In the second instance of this Court, all four defendants at first instance appealed, arguing that the judgment of the first instance did not comply with the legal requirements of China in the identification and admission of evidence. After this Court provided explanations, the parties still did not submit corresponding valid legal evidence for rebuttal. According to Article 2 of this Court's "Provisions on Evidence in Civil Proceedings", which states: "The parties have the responsibility to provide evidence to prove the facts on which their claims are based or the facts on which the opposing party's claims are rebutted. If there is no evidence or the evidence is insufficient to prove the party's factual allegations, the party bearing the burden of proof shall bear the adverse consequences." The four appellants should bear the legal consequences of failing to provide evidence. First, regarding the quantity of ore loss of 27,288 tons claimed by Baiyin Company, this quantity was obtained from actual measurements of the cross-boundary mining site by Baiyin Company's liquidation group as a member of the joint investigation team, before and after the two investigations organized by the local government, and then strictly calculated in accordance with the ore grade and calculation formula determined in the relevant geological report submitted by Team 106 and approved by the National Mineral Reserves Committee. Moreover, the factual report on the cross-boundary mining, including this data, was affirmed by the Longnan Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources and the Gansu Provincial Department of Land and Resources' three-level joint investigation team, and became one of the basic bases for the administrative penalty imposed by the Longnan Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources, carrying considerable authority. This data was a theoretical calculation result and should have been verified through on-site inspection. However, after the cross-boundary mining was discovered, the Huangzhu Ore Dressing Plant not only failed to cease the infringement and preserve the site, but also repeatedly carried out malicious obstruction acts such as blasting and sealing. The Longnan Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources repeatedly issued orders requiring it to cease the infringement and immediately clear the site, but the Huangzhu Ore Dressing Plant refused to clear the site and obstructed the relevant investigations, resulting in the inability to accurately verify the mineral loss to date. These blasting and sealing acts were a continuation of the tortious conduct in this case and the main reason for the inability to accurately verify the actual losses, and have been confirmed by valid administrative documents of the local and mineral resource management authorities. During the investigation and handling of the cross-boundary mining incident by the investigation team organized by the local government, Mao Dexian and the Huangzhu Ore Dressing Plant signed and affixed their official seals on the "Cross-Boundary Mining Investigation Plan View" issued by Baiyin Company's liquidation group, a member of the investigation team, thereby acknowledging their own tortious conduct and the scope and location of that conduct. However, in the litigation of this case, Mao Dexian refused to admit that the Huangzhu Ore Dressing Plant carried out the blasting and sealing acts and denied the connection between the plant's cross-boundary mining and the harmful consequences, which violated the principle of good faith. Therefore, this Court does not support this. As for the "Estimation Report" prepared by the First Geological Exploration Institute based on the entrustment of the Gansu Provincial Department of Land and Resources' three-level joint investigation team regarding the tortious facts, it also clearly stated that the 97-line stope could not be entered due to sealing, but the report did not mention the 105-line III2 stope, and some data necessary for loss calculation were not provided. The court of first instance did not adopt this "Estimation Report", which complies with the provisions of China's civil litigation evidence rules and is not improper. In the second instance of this Court, Team 106 submitted an application requesting that an authoritative department conduct an appraisal of the ore losses caused by the tort in this case. In this regard, this Court holds that, based on the facts of the case that have been ascertained, it is no longer possible to restore the historical appearance of the cross-boundary mining at that time, and there are no conditions for conducting a relevant appraisal in this case. Therefore, this Court does not grant the application. The judgment of the first instance determining the quantity of cross-boundary mined ore in this case as 27,288 tons and calculating the amount of tort damages in this case using the ore grade and calculation formula determined in the "Geological Exploration Report of the Lijia Valley Lead-Zinc Deposit in Cheng County, Gansu Province" submitted by Team 106 and approved by the National Mineral Reserves Committee in January 1988 complies with the basic requirements of China's civil litigation evidence rules and is not improper. This Court affirms it. Second, in their appeal arguments, the four appellants all submitted that the raw ore price, rather than the concentrate price, should be used when calculating the specific amount of loss. During the second instance, this Court, ex officio, visited and consulted with the Ministry of Land and Resources, the Longnan Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources, the Price Bureau, and other departments, but was unable to find exact direct evidence such as the market price or national guiding price of the raw ore involved. As previously stated, due to reasons attributable to the appellants, the stope could not be restored to its original state, and the conditions for a statutory appraisal do not exist in this case. The appellants have not submitted valid legal evidence for rebuttal. In accordance with the requirements of the evidence rules, the appellants should bear the legal consequences of failing to provide evidence. Therefore, the judgment of the first instance actually adopted the average value of the invoices for the prices of lead concentrate and zinc concentrate purchased by Baiyin Company in October 2006 (not 1996), the month when the cross-boundary mining was discovered, which complies with the requirements of this Court's civil litigation evidence rules, and this Court affirms it. Regarding the appellants' submissions that when calculating the specific amount of loss, the costs of mining, beneficiation, losses, management and transportation expenses, and taxes should be deducted, this Court holds that this case is a dispute over infringement of mining rights. The cross-boundary mining in this case is an illegal tortious act, different from ordinary lawful commercial transactions. This illegal act persisted for many years, causing enormous damage to state-owned mine resources, resulting in the loss of state-owned assets, and seriously harming the national interest. After the tortious act was discovered and the relevant national regulatory authorities repeatedly ordered the immediate cessation of the infringement, the infringers still obstructed the investigation and destroyed evidence through blasting, sealing, and other means, and have been subject to administrative penalties by the relevant state authorities. Therefore, the people's court should impose sanctions on such malicious tortious acts. After raw ore is extracted and processed through production procedures such as processing and transportation, it is converted into deep-processed products such as concentrates. Deducting necessary costs such as mining, transportation, labor wages, and taxes from the calculation of tort losses to arrive at net profit for compensation is a calculation method commonly used in damages disputes arising from ordinary contractual transactions. The tortious act of the parties in this case is completely different from ordinary ore mining transactions; it is a malicious infringement of state-owned assets, of a serious nature, causing incalculable losses to state-owned assets. Shifting the costs of such a malicious tortious act to the victim state-owned enterprise has neither legal basis nor reason. Moreover, after the court provided explanations in the first instance rebuttal and the second instance appeal, the appellants refused to provide relevant evidence of their own illegal cross-boundary mining costs. Therefore, this Court does not support this. Consequently, the appellants' appeal request for re-determination of the price and loss lacks factual and legal basis, cannot be established, and this Court does not support it.
